title: Configure and verify DHCP client and relay

questions.question: Which command can verify the active DHCP server that has assigned an IP address to the router?
choices: Router#show dhcp lease
Router#show ip dhcp lease
Router#show ip lease
Router#show ip interface

correct.explanation: show dhcp lease on a DHCP client router displays the active lease from the server that assigned the address.

incorrect.explanation: show ip dhcp lease is for routers acting as DHCP servers — a client router uses show dhcp lease.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using server-side show command on a DHCP client
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip dhcp lease is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (dhcp client): Router#show dhcp lease inspects the right table or state — Router#show ip dhcp lease shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: show ip lease is not the standard IOS client verification command — show dhcp lease is.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip lease is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (dhcp client): Router#show dhcp lease inspects the right table or state — Router#show ip lease shows unrelated information.

incorrect.explanation: show ip interface confirms interface status/IP but does not detail the DHCP server and lease timers like show dhcp lease.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Substituting interface status for DHCP lease details
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip interface is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (dhcp client): Router#show dhcp lease inspects the right table or state — Router#show ip interface shows unrelated information.

answerReview.examTip: Client router lease check → show dhcp lease. Server pool → show ip dhcp binding.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Offer packet of DHCP?
choices: The layer 3 destination is a unicast to the DHCP client.
The layer 2 destination is the MAC address of the DHCP client.
The layer 2 source is the MAC address of the server.
The layer 3 source is a link-local address of the client.

correct.explanation: The DHCP Offer is sent from the server MAC as the Layer 2 source — L3 may still be broadcast until the client has an IP.

incorrect.explanation: During DORA the client often has no IP yet — Offer is frequently broadcast at Layer 3, not unicast to client IP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting unicast L3 Offer before client has address
incorrect.whatItDoes: The layer 3 destination is a unicast to the DHCP client. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: The stem asks what gets learned (dhcp client). Switches record the source MAC on ingress — destination MAC is for lookup, not learning.

incorrect.explanation: Layer 2 destination is often broadcast (ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff) because the client may not have bound the offered IP yet.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Assuming Offer is always unicast to client MAC
incorrect.whatItDoes: The layer 2 destination is the MAC address of the DHCP client. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: The stem asks what gets learned (dhcp client). Switches record the source MAC on ingress — destination MAC is for lookup, not learning. Picking The layer 2 destination is the MAC address of the DHCP client. misses the exact behavior this stem tests.

incorrect.explanation: The Layer 3 source is the server address — link-local is not the standard Offer source on IPv4 DHCP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Claiming Offer L3 source is client link-local
incorrect.whatItDoes: The layer 3 source is a link-local address of the client. states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: This is a Layer 2 process (dhcp client). The layer 2 source is the MAC address of the server. uses Ethernet addresses — not IP headers.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP Offer → server MAC as L2 source; L2 dest often broadcast pre-ACK.

questions.question: Which command configure a DHCP relay agent on an interface to the DHCP server of 10.10.1.101?
choices: Router(config)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101
Router(config-if)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101
Router(config-if)#ip relay-agent 10.10.1.101
Router(config-if)#ip helper-address 10.10.1.101

correct.explanation: DHCP relay on a router/L3 SVI uses ip helper-address 10.10.1.101 under the client-facing interface to forward broadcasts to the server.

incorrect.explanation: ip dhcp server in global config is not the relay command — helper-address goes on the interface where clients sit.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Global dhcp server instead of interface helper-address
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Router(config-if)#ip helper-address 10.10.1.101 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ip dhcp server under interface is wrong syntax — relay uses ip helper-address.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Wrong interface DHCP command for relay
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-if)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101 points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Router(config-if)#ip helper-address 10.10.1.101 satisfies what this question tests — Router(config-if)#ip dhcp server 10.10.1.101 does not.

incorrect.explanation: ip relay-agent is not valid Cisco IOS syntax for DHCP relay — the command is ip helper-address.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config-if)#ip relay-agent 10.10.1.101 forwards DHCP broadcasts toward a remote server rather than acting as the DHCP server itself.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: DHCP roles (dhcp client): Router(config-if)#ip helper-address 10.10.1.101 matches who acts in this scenario — Router(config-if)#ip relay-agent 10.10.1.101 confuses relay/helper with server or client duties.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP relay → ip helper-address <server> on the client VLAN interface.

questions.question: Which DHCP field helps a DHCP server decide which scope to serve to the DHCP relay agent?
choices: CIADDR
GIADDR
SIADDR
CHADDR

correct.explanation: GIADDR (Gateway IP Address) in the DHCP request tells the server which subnet/scope the client is on via the relay agent.

incorrect.explanation: CIADDR is the client's current IP (renew/rebind) — empty in initial DISCOVER.
incorrect.whatItDoes: CIADDR points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", GIADDR satisfies what this question tests — CIADDR does not.

incorrect.explanation: SIADDR is the next-server IP (e.g. boot file server) — not the relay subnet hint.
incorrect.whatItDoes: SIADDR points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", GIADDR satisfies what this question tests — SIADDR does not.

incorrect.explanation: CHADDR is the client's hardware (MAC) address — not the subnet identifier.
incorrect.whatItDoes: CHADDR points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", GIADDR satisfies what this question tests — CHADDR does not.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP fields: CHADDR=MAC | GIADDR=relay interface IP (scope hint) | CIADDR=client IP on renew.

questions.question:
Network layout:
- Host A: 192.168.10.10/24 on VLAN 10 (no local DHCP server)
- Router R1 Gi0/0: 192.168.10.1 — needs ip helper-address toward remote DHCP
- Remote DHCP server: 10.0.0.5 on another subnet

what is required on the network to allow Host A to receive an IP address from the existing DHCP server?
choices: A second DHCP server on the Host A network
A DHCP relay agent on Router B interface Gi0/0
A DHCP relay agent on Switch A
A DHCP relay agent on Router A interface Gi0/0

correct.explanation: Configure ip helper-address <dhcp-server> on Router A Gi0/0 — the router facing the client subnet relays broadcasts to the remote server.

incorrect.explanation: A second local DHCP server is unnecessary — ip helper-address forwards to the existing server.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Second DHCP server instead of relay
incorrect.whatItDoes: A second DHCP server on the Host A network points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", A DHCP relay agent on Router A interface Gi0/0 satisfies what this question tests — A second DHCP server on the Host A network does not.

incorrect.explanation: The relay goes on Router A (client-facing router), not an unrelated Router B.
incorrect.whatItDoes: A DHCP relay agent on Router B interface Gi0/0 forwards DHCP broadcasts toward a remote server rather than acting as the DHCP server itself.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: DHCP roles (dhcp client): A DHCP relay agent on Router A interface Gi0/0 matches who acts in this scenario — A DHCP relay agent on Router B interface Gi0/0 confuses relay/helper with server or client duties.

incorrect.explanation: DHCP relay is a router L3 function — switches don't run ip helper-address.
incorrect.whatItDoes: A DHCP relay agent on Switch A forwards DHCP broadcasts toward a remote server rather than acting as the DHCP server itself.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: DHCP roles (dhcp client): A DHCP relay agent on Router A interface Gi0/0 matches who acts in this scenario — A DHCP relay agent on Switch A confuses relay/helper with server or client duties.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP relay: ip helper-address <ip> on the client-facing router interface — forwards UDP/67 broadcasts.

questions.question: Which command can diagnose DHCP relay agent messages on a router or switch?
choices: Router#debug dhcp
Router#show ip dhcp detail
Router#debug ip dhcp server packet
Router#debug ip dhcp

correct.explanation: debug ip dhcp server packet shows DHCP server packet flow — use on the server or relay for relay-agent diagnosis.

incorrect.explanation: debug dhcp is too broad/nonstandard — IOS uses debug ip dhcp variants.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#debug dhcp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Router#debug ip dhcp server packet satisfies what this question tests — Router#debug dhcp does not.

incorrect.explanation: show ip dhcp detail is not the standard debug — use debug ip dhcp server packet.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Show command for DHCP relay debug
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#show ip dhcp detail is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Router#debug ip dhcp server packet satisfies what this question tests — Router#show ip dhcp detail does not.

incorrect.explanation: debug ip dhcp alone is less specific — debug ip dhcp server packet targets relay/server packets.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Generic debug ip dhcp for relay packets
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router#debug ip dhcp points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Router#debug ip dhcp server packet satisfies what this question tests — Router#debug ip dhcp does not.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP debug: debug ip dhcp server events | debug ip dhcp server packet — always undebug all after.

questions.question: Identify DHCPv6 used for when a network is configured for Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC)?
choices: Stateful configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing
Configuration of clients with the IPv6 network IDs
Configuration of clients with IPv6 options
Stateless configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing

correct.explanation: With SLAAC, hosts self-assign addresses — DHCPv6 delivers options (DNS, domain name) without assigning the address.

incorrect.explanation: Stateful DHCPv6 assigns addresses — SLAAC networks use DHCPv6 for stateless options.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Stateful configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): Configuration of clients with IPv6 options matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — Stateful configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: SLAAC derives the address from the prefix + EUI-64 — DHCPv6 options don't supply the network ID for addressing.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: DHCPv6 supplies network ID in SLAAC
incorrect.whatItDoes: Configuration of clients with the IPv6 network IDs states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): Configuration of clients with IPv6 options matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — Configuration of clients with the IPv6 network IDs breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: Stateless DHCPv6 in SLAAC means no address lease — only options are provided.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Stateless addressing via DHCPv6 in SLAAC
incorrect.whatItDoes: Stateless configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): Configuration of clients with IPv6 options matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — Stateless configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

answerReview.examTip: SLAAC + DHCPv6 = stateless (options only) | Stateful DHCPv6 assigns full addresses.

questions.question: The DHCP server in the network went down. What happens to clients that have obtained IP addresses from the DHCP server?
choices: They lose their IP address immediately.
They lose their IP address after one-half of their lease has expired.
They lose their IP address after seven-eighths of their lease has expired.
They lose their IP address after their entire lease has expired.

correct.explanation: Clients keep the leased IP until the full lease expires — even if the server is down, until T1/T2 timers fail.

incorrect.explanation: Addresses are not revoked immediately when the server fails — the lease timer still runs.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Immediate IP loss on server down
incorrect.whatItDoes: They lose their IP address immediately. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", They lose their IP address after their entire lease has expired. satisfies what this question tests — They lose their IP address immediately. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Half-lease (T1) triggers renewal, not immediate loss — client keeps using the IP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: IP lost at half lease on server down
incorrect.whatItDoes: They lose their IP address after one-half of their lease has expired. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", They lose their IP address after their entire lease has expired. satisfies what this question tests — They lose their IP address after one-half of their lease has expired. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Seven-eighths (T2) starts rebind, not relinquish — loss happens at full lease expiry.
incorrect.whatItDoes: They lose their IP address after seven-eighths of their lease has expired. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", They lose their IP address after their entire lease has expired. satisfies what this question tests — They lose their IP address after seven-eighths of their lease has expired. does not.

answerReview.examTip: DHCP lease timers: T1 = 50% renew | T2 = 87.5% rebind | 100% = lease expires.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about stateful DHCPv6?
choices: Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID.
Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID, host ID, and default router.
Stateful DHCPv6 communicates via broadcasts.
Stateful DHCPv6 works in conjunction with SLAAC.

correct.explanation: Stateful DHCPv6 assigns both network prefix and host interface ID — full address management like DHCPv4.

incorrect.explanation: Default router info typically comes from RA (SLAAC) — stateful DHCPv6 focuses on address assignment.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID, host ID, and default router. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID. satisfies what this question tests — Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID, host ID, and default router. does not.

incorrect.explanation: DHCPv6 uses multicast (FF02::1:2), not IPv4-style broadcasts.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Stateful DHCPv6 communicates via broadcasts. describes flooding the frame to multiple ports in the VLAN.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID. satisfies what this question tests — Stateful DHCPv6 communicates via broadcasts. does not.

incorrect.explanation: SLAAC uses RA for addresses — stateful DHCPv6 replaces SLAAC addressing, not works alongside it for the same host.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Stateful DHCPv6 works with SLAAC addressing
incorrect.whatItDoes: Stateful DHCPv6 works in conjunction with SLAAC. states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID. satisfies what this question tests — Stateful DHCPv6 works in conjunction with SLAAC. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Stateful DHCPv6: ipv6 dhcp pool + address dhcp on client — full address lease like DHCPv4.

questions.question: Which command configure a router interface to obtain its IP address via a stateful DHCPv6?
choices: RouterA(config)#ipv6 address dhcp gi 0/0
RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcpv6
RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcp
RouterA(config)#ipv6 address stateless

correct.explanation: On the interface: ipv6 address dhcp — obtains a stateful DHCPv6 address from the server.

incorrect.explanation: ipv6 address dhcp is an interface command, not global config with gi 0/0.
incorrect.whatItDoes: RouterA(config)#ipv6 address dhcp gi 0/0 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcp matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — RouterA(config)#ipv6 address dhcp gi 0/0 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: Correct keyword is dhcp, not dhcpv6 — enter under config-if.
incorrect.whatItDoes: RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcpv6 states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcp matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcpv6 breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

incorrect.explanation: ipv6 address stateless is not the stateful command — use ipv6 address dhcp.
incorrect.whatItDoes: RouterA(config)#ipv6 address stateless states an IPv6 address, prefix length, or assignment method that may not follow shortening rules.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: IPv6 addressing (dhcp client): RouterA(config-if)#ipv6 address dhcp matches prefix, shortening, or assignment rules — RouterA(config)#ipv6 address stateless breaks IPv6 syntax or prefix length.

answerReview.examTip: IPv6 addressing modes: autoconfig (SLAAC) | dhcp (stateful) | dhcp rapid-commit (faster stateful).

questions.question: What happens if you delete a current lease on the DHCP server?
choices: The server will contact the client to immediately relinquish the IP address.
The client will immediately renew its lease for the current IP address.
The server will offer the IP address to another node, which will cause a duplicate address.
The server will offer the IP address to another node, at which time the original client will relinquish the IP address.

correct.explanation: Deleting a lease lets the server offer that IP to another client — the original holder may still use it until lease expiry → duplicate IP risk.

incorrect.explanation: The server does not force the old client to release immediately — the client may still use the address.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The server will contact the client to immediately relinquish the IP address. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", The server will offer the IP address to another node, which will cause a duplicate address. satisfies what this question tests — The server will contact the client to immediately relinquish the IP address. does not.

incorrect.explanation: The original client does not auto-renew a deleted lease — it keeps using the IP until T1/T2/expiry.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The client will immediately renew its lease for the current IP address. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", The server will offer the IP address to another node, which will cause a duplicate address. satisfies what this question tests — The client will immediately renew its lease for the current IP address. does not.

incorrect.explanation: The original client does not politely relinquish when another gets the same IP — conflict results.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The server will offer the IP address to another node, at which time the original client will relinquish the IP address. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: DHCP message order (dhcp client): The server will offer the IP address to another node, which will cause a duplicate address. is the step this stem describes — The server will offer the IP address to another node, at which time the original client will relinquish the IP address. is another DORA phase.

answerReview.examTip: Never delete active leases casually — wait for natural expiry or confirm the client released the address.

questions.question: What happens at the client when the lease for an IP address reaches seven-eighths of the lease cycle?
choices: The DHCP client will perform a DHCP rebinding.
Nothing. The DHCP client will retain the lease.
The DHCP client will renew its lease.
The DHCP client will relinquish the use of the IP address.

correct.explanation: At 7/8 (87.5%) of the lease, the client enters REBIND — broadcasts to any available DHCP server.

incorrect.explanation: At 7/8 the client actively rebinds — it does not passively retain without trying other servers.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Nothing. The DHCP client will retain the lease. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", The DHCP client will perform a DHCP rebinding. satisfies what this question tests — Nothing. The DHCP client will retain the lease. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Renewal (T1) happens at 50% of lease — 7/8 is rebind, not renew.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The DHCP client will renew its lease. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for dhcp client.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", The DHCP client will perform a DHCP rebinding. satisfies what this question tests — The DHCP client will renew its lease. does not.

incorrect.explanation: The client rebinds at 7/8 — it only relinquishes if the lease fully expires without success.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The DHCP client will relinquish the use of the IP address. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "dhcp client", The DHCP client will perform a DHCP rebinding. satisfies what this question tests — The DHCP client will relinquish the use of the IP address. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Lease timeline: 50% = RENEW (to original server) | 87.5% = REBIND (any server) | 100% = expire.
